cells.tense: The direction is set and the shape of it is clear from where you stand.
cells.ask: Say the direction out loud to the people it will move — one sentence, no defending it after — then take the next concrete step this week.
cells.core:
You can see how the pieces fit and you're steering by what you see. The direction you picked didn't get reasoned into place — it landed, and it's been holding since. That's the balance here: what you saw doing the pointing, and the shape of it staying clear while you move.

What keeps it is not more certainty. It's letting the direction carry weight. Some of the strength around you is already available — people who'd hold part of this if they knew what it was. You don't have to prove the direction to anyone. Say what it is and let it stand. What you feed next is the moving, not the watching. Pick up the next real step, and let the people who'd back it know where you're headed.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering by what you see, and the shape holds.
cells.verb: Choosing which direction to move toward

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that hasn't been written yet, and the bracing is the work now.
cells.ask: Pick the one direction people are already acting on, and let the other three wait untouched for a week — one decision, made once, not reviewed.
cells.core:
You can see the whole thing, and lately you see it ahead of time. Every fork gets read before it arrives, every option compared, and the comparing has become the steering. There's a future in your head where all of it is finally settled, and you're living there — which means the direction that's actually live keeps getting re-examined instead of walked.

What's left when everything is this full is a choice, not more looking. You can afford not to know the rest for now; knowing isn't the missing piece. Take the one direction already moving and let it move. The others can sit. What you're pointed at doesn't need defending before it's real. Let one path be walked while the others wait their turn.
cells.sheetLine: You're comparing every fork and walking none of them.
cells.verb: Choosing which direction to move toward

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you already walked through, still reading it as closed.
cells.ask: Put one direction into a single plain sentence, said to yourself or one person, then take one small step toward it this week — no verdict on how it goes.
cells.core:
You can read the pattern fine. What isn't happening is the pointing. The direction doesn't get named, so nothing gets aimed, and it looks like not knowing which way to go. Not knowing isn't what's missing — it's letting the choice become a choosable thing.

Nothing has to be forced into place for that. Direction comes back the way growth does: care that doesn't exhaust, holding a space without gripping it. Start by saying what you want, plainly, to yourself or to one person. One sentence is enough. Then one small step, and no verdict on it afterward. The path doesn't need your certainty to exist; it needs the first move to be made.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the pattern. You've stopped pointing at any of it.
cells.verb: Choosing which direction to move toward

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in, and someone else is getting the credit.
cells.ask: Claim one direction in front of another person — say it was your call, not the situation's — out loud, once, and let it stand.
cells.core:
You are already steering. The pattern gets read, the direction gets set, the people around you move accordingly — and it gets described as the situation, the timing, what had to happen. It's all still running quietly. What isn't: the act of calling it yours out loud.

What's underneath is simpler than the story you tell about it. Not the room, not the moment — you, deciding, and calling the deciding something else. You don't have to earn the credit or explain it; just stop handing it away. One direction, one sentence: this was your call. Say it to someone who saw it happen. What holds without forcing is what's real here, and this is yours to say.
cells.sheetLine: The steering is already happening. You keep calling it the situation.
cells.verb: Choosing which direction to move toward

attempts.check: The one claim the record does not support is a specific past room where saying the direction went badly — that is the template, not the kernel, and the Too Little cell stays forward-facing instead. A reader could reasonably say the pattern-seeing was never theirs to name, or that the direction is genuinely still open; the ask, deciding one thing people are already waiting on, is useful even if my read is wrong because it produces a real decision and teaches where the decision actually lives. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything like 'you already see the whole thing,' which flatters the reader and overrules the person; it is cut.
